A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SciLitLLM work. Their main texts, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material. Internal numerical inconsistencies in v4 do not prevent identifying the changes.

before.justification: V3 reports original model evaluations and ablations in Tables 2–6, with detailed SciAssess results in Appendix E. Table 3 distinguishes original results from borrowed baseline scores.

after.justification: V4 retains those original experiments and adds filtering-threshold results, contamination analysis, and human evaluation of dataset quality in Appendices C, G, and H.

M1.justification: The CPT-plus-SFT pipeline, instruction synthesis, deduplication, quality filters, and model configurations remain unchanged. The introduction's Llama3-7B reference becomes Llama3-8B, matching v3's existing method description. Newly tested filtering thresholds are sensitivity experiments, not changes to the adopted method.

E1.justification: Training corpora, scientific domains, instruction tasks, and benchmark coverage remain unchanged. The contamination-cleaned evaluation subset and human-rated samples come from existing datasets; these introduce evaluation procedures rather than new domain or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds an internal comparison variant trained with Infinity-Instruct plus SciLitIns without SciRIFF. The external baseline models in Tables 2 and 3 remain unchanged; SciTulu's reordered column does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: V4 adds substantial evaluation procedures: alternative SFT recipes, CPT filtering at 15%, 25%, and 35%, contamination detection using three randomly sampled 50-character substrings per evaluation instance, and full-versus-clean SciAssess evaluation. Appendix H adds 50 CPT and 50 SFT samples independently scored by four annotators. Existing main training budgets and benchmark procedures are retained.

E4.justification: V4 expands the SFT ablation to isolate SciLitIns without SciRIFF, adds filtering-threshold sensitivity analysis, examines training/evaluation contamination and its performance impact, and validates automated quality scores against human judgments. These address several previously untested questions about component effects and data reliability.

E5.justification: Appendix H introduces inter-rater reliability reporting through averaged Spearman correlations for human-human and human-filter agreement. Neither version reports repeated training runs, seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the main benchmark results.

E6.justification: V4 adds SciLitIns-only ablation scores of 50.2/54.8, threshold results, contamination and clean-set results, and human-agreement scores. Existing benchmark tables retain their values; the prose corrects the 14B SciAssess margin from 4.6 to 4.4 percentage points. New results contain inconsistencies: Table 7 reports 54.06 for the 25% threshold's MaScQA score versus 59.27 in Table 2, while Table 10's full-set means of 51.6/59.0 differ from Table 3's 51.7/58.2 without explanation.

T1.justification: The existing Levenshtein-based similarity definition is retained. Neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs, and v4's new empirical agreement measures do not introduce substantive mathematical theory.

C1.justification: The scientific contributions and headline performance claims remain intact. However, the abstract narrows the stated released outputs from code, model weights, and the synthetic dataset to code and model weights only.

C2.justification: V4 adds substantive interpretations concerning SciLitIns/SciRIFF complementarity, noise tolerance suggested by modest filtering gains, the filtering quality-versus-quantity tradeoff, contamination's purportedly negligible impact, and agreement with human quality judgments. The data-volume limitation also expands to discuss disciplinary underrepresentation and the difficulty of scaling without sacrificing quality.

D1.justification: V4 removes the SciLitIns download link and the reproducibility statement's promise to release it after administrative procedures. Model access changes to a collection link, and the anonymous-availability wording is removed. Core prompts, hyperparameters, hardware, and training-time information remain. The PDFs do not establish actual withdrawal of any resource.

R1.justification: V4 adds citations including S2ORC, Dolma, PaLM, and several molecular-modeling and recommendation studies. The main positioning against scientific pretraining and instruction tuning remains intact. Moving related work, changing Team to Qwen, and updating publication metadata do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: The complete related-work section moves from the main text to Appendix A, changing the narrative sequence. Performance analysis, ablation discussion, and the data-volume limitation receive substantial paragraph-level expansion and rewriting. V4 also adds acknowledgements and updates conference headers and author-contact formatting.

P2.justification: Figures 6 and 7 move from separate appendix locations into a shared main-text row; Figure 6 gains a percentage axis and expanded caption. Tables 2–6 receive labeling, emphasis, ordering, or structural changes. Four new tables present threshold, contamination, clean-set, and human-agreement analyses. The detailed SciAssess table is retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V4 adds useful ablation and human-validation evidence absent from v3. However, Table 7's averages do not match its printed entries, undermining the claimed optimal threshold, and Table 10's full-set scores conflict with Table 3 without an explained setting change. Dataset-access documentation also becomes less complete. These unresolved reliability and reproducibility tradeoffs prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
